content: Chronic stress refers to a state of stress that persists over an extended period or occurs frequently. This type of stress can have detrimental effects on both physical and mental health. Chronic stress may arise from various sources, such as ongoing family conflicts, challenging academic environments, overly demanding schedules, or prolonged illnesses. The symptoms associated with chronic stress are diverse and can include disordered eating patterns, gastrointestinal disturbances, headaches, back pain, insomnia, anxiety, depression, and episodes of anger. In severe cases, chronic stress may escalate to panic attacks or even develop into a panic disorder. There are several strategies to manage chronic stress effectively. These include engaging in regular physical exercise, maintaining a balanced and nutritious diet, practicing stress management techniques, utilizing relaxation methods, ensuring adequate sleep, and participating in enjoyable and calming hobbies. A diet rich in magnesium may be particularly beneficial for individuals with low magnesium levels or those suffering from magnesium deficiency, as this mineral plays a role in stress regulation. Chronic stress itself can contribute to magnesium deficiency, which may perpetuate the stress cycle and lead to additional adverse health conditions associated with insufficient magnesium levels. This deficiency can exacerbate the negative effects of chronic stress on the body. Recent findings indicate a significant increase in the number of individuals experiencing chronic stress. Among these cases, a substantial proportion report suffering from insomnia. A review of scientific literature examining the relationship between stress and disease has revealed that stress is a contributing factor in the onset or exacerbation of depression and cardiovascular disease. Furthermore, stress has been shown to accelerate the progression of conditions such as HIV/AIDS.
